description: Renovate updates go.mod and go.sum by calling `go get`, which ADDS the new sums and leaves the superseded ones behind. Any lane asserting that `go mod tidy` produces no diff then fails on go.sum alone, for a module that is perfectly sound, with a message naming no file -- so it reads like a defect in the dependency rather than leftover bookkeeping. Twenty-eight pull requests failed that way in two days: eleven on the morning of 2026-09-02, seventeen that evening on purego v0.10.2 -> v0.11.0. go-macos/hotkey#12 is one of them, and the repair commit (9c14c321) deleted four go.sum lines and touched nothing else. gomodTidy has Renovate run `go mod tidy` itself, before the pull request exists, so the drift never reaches a branch. It is a no-op in a repository with no Go module. gomodUpdateImportPaths is here to UNBLOCK that tidy, not for import paths: lib/modules/manager/gomod/artifacts.ts skips tidy outright when updateType is major unless this option is set, and Renovate calls a 0.x minor bump a major -- which is every case that failed here, hence the branch names ending -0.x. Its own commands are filtered to newMajor > 1, so for a 0.x dependency it emits nothing and never installs marwan-at-work/mod; measured, gomodTidy alone changed nothing on go-macos/appkit#2.

packageRules.description: One pull request per repository for everything non-breaking, rather than one per dependency. Merging them singly means every merge rebases the others and restarts their checks: one run over an organisation of 34 repositories updated 109 branches and merged 2. Grouped, a repository needs one round of checks instead of dozens.

Never auto-merge the Go toolchain, and never let it ride in somebody else's group. A rule that says automerge:false for one dependency is defeated by grouping, because Renovate decides automerge per BRANCH: go 1.27.0 rode into seven repositories inside a branch called renovate/github-actions, whose other dependency was actions/setup-go. Ungrouped, it gets a branch of its own and this setting governs it. It matters because go1.27.0 miscompiles on loong64 (golang/go#81000, bisected on real hardware to 3fdac6780b): go-gfx/gfx fails that lane and stayed open only because the lane failed, which is the CI gate holding rather than this rule. A repository without such a lane sees nothing.
